question: The oesophagus and the lining of the mouth are also covered with:
solution:
The correct answer is __**squamous epithelium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Squamous epithelium** is a type of epithelial tissue composed of flat, scale-like cells.
 
• It lines the **oesophagus** and the **oral cavity**, providing a protective layer against mechanical stress and abrasion.
 
• The cells in squamous epithelium are tightly packed, creating a barrier to protect underlying tissues.
 
• This type of epithelium is also found in other areas of the body such as the **skin** (epidermis), and the lining of the **vagina** and **anal canal**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Epithelial Tissue:**

 
 
• Epithelial tissues are one of the four basic types of animal tissues, including connective, muscle, and nervous tissues.
 
• They cover the body surfaces, line body cavities, and form glands.
 
• Epithelial cells are closely packed with minimal intercellular material and are tightly bound together by special junctions.
 
 
 
• **Cuboidal Epithelium:**
 
 
• Composed of cube-shaped cells.
 
• Commonly found in glandular tissues and in the lining of the kidney tubules.
 
• Involved in absorption, secretion, and excretion processes.
 
 
 
• **Ciliated Columnar Epithelium:**
 
 
• Contains column-like cells with cilia on the surface.
 
• Lines the respiratory tract and the fallopian tubes, helping in the movement of mucus or eggs.
 
 
 
• **Glandular Epithelium:**
 
 
• Specialized for secretion and forms the glands.
 
• Can be unicellular (goblet cells) or multicellular (salivary glands).
